issues.description:
Element: Pneumatic.openValve() vs Pneumatic.releaseValve()
Problem statement (UML) declares an interface Pneumatic with an abstract method openValve() (and raisePressure(int)). The template Pneumatic.java is blank (only package declaration). The solution repository defines the Pneumatic interface with a method named releaseValve() (and raisePressure(int)), but the solution's implementing classes LaunchedDropdownTower and LaunchedRollerCoaster implement a method named openValve(). This name mismatch between the interface (releaseValve) and the UML + implementing classes (openValve) will cause confusion for students about which method to implement and will produce compilation errors in the solution code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix (match UML): rename the method releaseValve() in solution/src/de/tum/in/ase/Pneumatic.java to openValve(), and ensure the interface and all implementing classes (LaunchedDropdownTower, LaunchedRollerCoaster) declare/override openValve(). Alternatively, if releaseValve() is intentionally preferred, update the UML/problem statement to list releaseValve() instead of openValve() and update the implementing classes to override releaseValve().

issues.description: The UML/problem statement defines a Pneumatic interface method named openValve(). In the solution, the Pneumatic interface declares releaseValve() (src/de/tum/in/ase/Pneumatic.java) while the implementing classes (LaunchedRollerCoaster and LaunchedDropdownTower) define and annotate openValve(). This yields two different identifiers for the same conceptual operation (opening the valve): the problem statement and implementations expect openValve(), but the solution interface uses releaseValve(). Students reading the UML will expect an openValve() method to implement or invoke; the mismatch prevents a clear mapping and introduces a compilation inconsistency between the interface and its implementors.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier consistent across artifacts. Rename the Pneumatic interface method releaseValve() to openValve() in src/de/tum/in/ase/Pneumatic.java to match the UML and the implementing classes, or alternatively rename the openValve() methods in the implementing classes to releaseValve() and update the UML/problem statement accordingly. Prefer aligning the interface to the UML (openValve()) to minimize changes to implementations and student expectations.
